entry.summary: No visa needed before travel. Permission to stay up to 90 days is given on arrival by the immigration officer.
entry.max_stay: Up to 90 days, as the officer decides
entry.pre_arrival: Be ready to show accommodation, return flights and contacts in Ireland. At least one blank passport page.
entry.other: Ireland isn't in Schengen and doesn't accept Schengen visas. Work or study needs a visa applied for before leaving Australia.

tourism.route: Visa-exempt visitor entry and landing permission
tourism.detail: Australian passport holders are visa-exempt, but the border officer decides admission and may grant up to three months for the declared visitor purpose.
tourism.next: Carry onward travel, accommodation, funds, insurance and a clear itinerary.

meetings.route: Visa-exempt entry for declared business activity
meetings.detail: Meetings, contract signing and business discussions fit the published short-business framework. The short-stay C visa application itself is unnecessary for an Australian, but the activity and documentary boundaries still matter at entry.
meetings.next: Carry an Irish host invitation describing the meetings and confirming that no local work will occur.

conference.detail: Attendance fits the conference purpose. The published conference permission does not allow paid or unpaid work, so a panel, talk, workshop or facilitation role must be classified separately.
conference.next: Register as an attendee and ask the organiser to classify any programmed role as short work or performance.

unpaid-speaking.route: Declared short-business activity for one single work period of no more than 14 days
unpaid-speaking.detail: An unpaid program role is still work; attendance permission alone does not cover speaking. The published short-business framework permits a single work period of 14 days or less, subject to purpose and border evidence.
unpaid-speaking.next: Have the host document zero fee, every covered expense, dates and duties; for 15 days or more obtain written classification from Immigration Service Delivery.

paid-speaking.route: Short-business or performance activity for no more than 14 days; possible Atypical Working Scheme for 15 to 90 days
paid-speaking.detail: A short paid speaking or performance engagement may fit the single 14-day work window. The Atypical Working Scheme can support specialised longer work, but its registered-host, employment-contract and salary requirements mean self-employed or loosely structured speaking tours are not assumed eligible.
paid-speaking.next: Have one Irish host obtain written classification of the complete tour, contract, euro salary or fee, expenses and duration before booking.

book-launch.route: Business meetings plus separately classified speaking, performance and sales activity
book-launch.detail: Publisher and rights meetings are business activity. A reading, launch appearance or signing may be work, while direct retail introduces separate commercial, customs and tax questions.
book-launch.next: Use an Irish publisher or bookseller for sales and split rights meetings, appearance duties, royalties and retail in the invitation.

ai-teaching.route: Single short-business work period up to 14 days, Atypical Working Scheme for 15 to 90 days or an eligible visiting-academic arrangement
ai-teaching.detail: A brief workshop or lecture may use the short-work window. Longer specialised teaching may require Atypical approval; an institution-led visiting-academic route can apply to eligible visits under 12 months when the Irish and overseas institutions document the arrangement.
ai-teaching.next: Have the institution identify whether the role is a guest lecture, short training, atypical employment or visiting-academic exchange before advertising it.

remote-work.detail: The official short-stay catalogue does not publish routine overseas remote work as a visitor purpose, and visitor permission does not generally authorise paid or unpaid work. Irish PAYE rules can also arise for duties exercised in Ireland.
remote-work.next: Do not use visitor entry as a routine remote-work base without written immigration and tax advice.

entrepreneur.detail: STEP requires good character, at least €50,000 funding for the first founder, an innovative business proposal and a €350 application fee. Successful applicants must work on the business full-time and may not take other employment.
entrepreneur.next: Test the venture against the innovation criteria and secure funding before submitting the proposal for quarterly evaluation.

trade.route: Meetings and negotiation, one short work period up to 14 days, Atypical approval or Contract for Services Employment Permit
trade.detail: Trade discussions are easy. Longer delivery under a foreign undertaking's one-to-one contract with an Irish entity may use a Contract for Services Employment Permit, normally requiring at least six months with the overseas employer and an application at least 12 weeks before the proposed start. Solo self-employed fit is not assumed.
trade.next: Classify the trip as negotiation, short delivery or contracted service, then have the Irish customer begin the correct host process.

artist.route: Short performance activity, Atypical Working Scheme or Sport and Cultural Employment Permit
artist.detail: A paid or unpaid performance may fit the single 14-day work window. Longer cultural employment can require Atypical approval or an employment permit with an Irish contract and host.
artist.next: Have the organiser document the performance, rehearsals, fee, expenses and duration and start any permit process at least 12 weeks ahead.

mixed-mission.route: Visa-exempt entry with written classification for each work component
mixed-mission.detail: Tourism, meetings and attendance can coexist, but speaking, teaching, performance, sales and service delivery keep separate activity rules and time limits.
mixed-mission.next: Nominate one Irish lead host and obtain written classification from Immigration Service Delivery or the Department of Enterprise where any work boundary is unclear.

filming.route: Ask the Embassy of Ireland, Yarralumla
filming.detail: No official statement on this activity was read. Easy entry isn't permission to work.
filming.next: Ask the Embassy of Ireland, Yarralumla which visa covers it, in writing.

money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Euro. Ireland is a member of the European Union (EU). If you're travelling between Ireland and any non-EU country, you must declare amounts over 10,000 euros or equivalent. This covers all forms of currency, not only cash. You'll have to pay a fine when you enter or leave Ireland if you: don't declare this money give incorrect information You don't need to declare currency if you're travelling between EU countries. ATMs are widely available. Ask your bank before you leave if your card will work in Ireland.

baseline_unverified.host_unlock: An Irish organiser invitation supports the short-business or performance purpose. For the Atypical Working Scheme, the Irish host must be registered and provide the contract, duties, salary in euros and duration.
baseline_unverified.fastest_entry: Travel visa-exempt and request landing permission for the declared tourism, business or event purpose; the immigration officer may grant up to three months.
baseline_unverified.before_departure: Carry purpose evidence, funds, insurance, accommodation and host invitations. If any work lasts 15 to 90 days, obtain Atypical Working Scheme approval outside Ireland before travel and allow at least 20 working days.
baseline_unverified.useful_stay: Landing permission may allow up to three months, but work is separately limited: one single work period of 14 days or less unless prior approval or an employment permit applies.
documents: Invitation stating duties, dates, fee and every covered cost
Original contract and prior work approval where applicable
steps: Travel visa-exempt with the Australian passport and evidence supporting the declared purpose.
Build one dated schedule of meetings, attendance, talks, teaching, performances, sales and payments.
Use the published single work period of no more than 14 days only where the host has documented the correct short-business or performance purpose.
For work lasting 15 to 90 days, test the Atypical Working Scheme and allow at least 20 working days after a complete application.
For longer contracted services or cultural employment, begin the employment-permit process at least 12 weeks before the proposed start.
